deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is §6.5 of the 'laïus' on crystals, with S = Spec C. On p.68 Grothendieck computes the cohomology of O on the stratifying site of an algebraic C-scheme X using a Čech–Alexander-type spectral sequence. Its E_2 term is built from the cosimplicial formal scheme ν ↦ (X^{ν+1})^∧, the formal completion of X^{ν+1} along the diagonal. For X proper he uses Mittag-Leffler and GAGA to move the computation to the analytic side, getting H^*(X_strat, O) ≅ H^*(X^an, F^*_{X^an}).

This page.
1. He defines the analytic complex of sheaves F^*_{X^an} 'in the same way as in the algebraic case': F^ν(U) = Γ(U^{ν+1}_{/U}, O). Here U runs over the open sets of X^an and U^{ν+1}_{/U} is the formal completion of U^{ν+1} along the diagonal. The differentials are the alternating sums of the cosimplicial coface maps.
2. Conjecture: for every complex analytic space 𝒳 (possibly singular, possibly non-reduced), the complex F^*_𝒳, augmented by C_𝒳 → F^0, is a resolution of the constant sheaf C. This is a 'formal Poincaré lemma via formal neighbourhoods of diagonals', with no smoothness hypothesis and no ambient smooth space. Consequence (in brackets): H^*(𝒳_strat, O) = H^*(𝒳, C).
3. Heuristic: it 'seems plausible by looking at the formal fibres of the sheaves', i.e. by checking stalks of the completed cosimplicial rings.
4. Theorem (conditional): if X is proper over C and the conjecture holds for X^an, then H^*(X_strat, O_{X_strat}) ≅ H^*(X^an, C) canonically. This follows immediately from p.68.

Next page. If X embeds in a smooth Y, the map from crystalline to stratifying cohomology is also an isomorphism. He then asks a general problem: is crystalline cohomology of a crystal equal to its stratifying cohomology?

What the conjecture says in modern terms. Stratifying cohomology of a singular X is the cohomology of the Čech nerve of X → X_dR (with X ×_{X_dR} X = completion of X×X along Δ). Since X → X_dR is not formally smooth when X is singular, it is not a priori a cover, so the conjecture is a genuine statement. It asks whether X itself can serve as its own 'ambient' in the Čech–Alexander computation of infinitesimal/de Rham cohomology.

Check.
- Non-reduced case: for X = Spec C[ε], the diagonal ideal is nilpotent, so the completions equal X^{ν+1}. The complex is then the Amitsur complex of C → C[ε], which is exact with H^0 = C. Consistent.
- General case: the conjecture very plausibly follows by a standard bicosimplicial argument. Locally embed X in a smooth Y and form the double object (X^{a+1} × Y^{b+1})^∧ along Δ_X.
  - The b-direction has a section (X → Y), so it contracts to the stratifying complex of X.
  - The a-direction is the Čech nerve of X ×_{X_dR} Ŷ → Ŷ. Locally this is C[[y,t]]/(f(y−t)) over C[[y]], which is flat and faithfully flat (y = x + t substitution). Hence the a-direction is exact and reduces to the Čech–Alexander complex of Y along X.
  - That complex computes Hartshorne's formal de Rham cohomology, which is ≅ Betti cohomology (Hartshorne 1975, with roots in Grothendieck's 1966 letter/IHES note).
  So the conjecture is essentially equivalent to H_strat(X) ≅ H_inf(X) ≅ H_dR^{Hartshorne}(X) ≅ H(X^an, C).
errors: On p.68 the spectral sequence is labelled as abutting to H^*(X_cris, O_{X_cris}), but its E_2 term (the cosimplicial completions of X^{ν+1} along the diagonal of X itself) computes stratifying cohomology. For singular X the identification with crystalline/infinitesimal cohomology is exactly what the next page treats separately (via an embedding in a smooth Y). The page itself is consistent, writing H^*(X_strat,…).

The bracketed consequence 'pour X propre' is stated for the analytic space 𝒳; properness is irrelevant for the analytic statement. It is needed only for the algebraic comparison via GAGA/Mittag-Leffler, as in the Theorem.

The heuristic 'en regardant les fibres formelles' is not a proof. The conjecture is not automatic, since X → X_dR is not formally smooth for singular X. A flatness/bicomplex argument through a local smooth embedding seems needed.

ideas.what: Analytic Čech–Alexander complex F^*: U ↦ Γ((U^{ν+1})^∧_Δ, O) on an analytic space
ideas.modern_name: Čech–Alexander complex / functions on the Čech nerve of X → X_dR (formal groupoid of the diagonal)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals, 1966–68); Berthelot for the crystalline Čech–Alexander complex; Simpson for the de Rham stack
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968), stratifying/infinitesimal topoi; analytic version unsure

ideas.what: Conjecture: for every (singular, non-reduced) complex analytic space the formal-diagonal complex resolves C
ideas.modern_name: Formal Poincaré lemma for singular spaces; stratifying (Čech nerve of X→X_dR) cohomology = Betti cohomology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Comparison infinitesimal/Hartshorne de Rham = Betti: Grothendieck (idea, 1966), Hartshorne (1975), Bhatt–de Jong / Bhatt (2011–12) for crystalline = de Rham. Stratifying version with X as its own ambient: unsure
ideas.where_published: Possibly remarks in 'Crystals…' §4–5 on stratifying vs infinitesimal topos; unsure

ideas.what: Conditional theorem: X proper over C ⇒ H^*(X_strat, O) ≅ H^*(X^an, C) via GAGA and Mittag-Leffler
ideas.where_published: Analogous comparison theorem for infinitesimal cohomology in 'Crystals…' (1968)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly conjectures that the stratifying (formal-diagonal Čech nerve) complex of an arbitrary singular analytic space resolves C, using X itself as ambient, without a smooth embedding. Literature comparisons (Hartshorne, Bhatt–de Jong, Bhatt) go through a smooth ambient or the infinitesimal/crystalline site. An explicit treatment of 'H_strat = H_inf' for singular X in char 0 (equivalently, X→X_dR being of effective cohomological descent for O) is not something I can point to.
missed.quote: Conjecture Pour tout espace analytique 𝒳, le complexe F^*_𝒳 est une résolution du faisceau C_𝒳 (via l'augmentation évidente)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a concrete descent question about X → X_dR for singular (derived) schemes. It bears on computing de Rham cohomology via the Čech nerve of the diagonal (cf. derived de Rham, de Rham stacks of Gaitsgory–Rozenblyum, analytic de Rham stacks). It likely has a short proof via flatness of X×_{X_dR}Ŷ → Ŷ, but that proof seems not to be on record as an answer to this question.

deep.surprise_reason: The ingredients (Čech–Alexander, stratifying topos, comparison with Betti) are known and credited to Grothendieck/Hartshorne/Berthelot. The specific conjecture is a precise, apparently unrecorded formulation of descent along X → X_dR for singular analytic spaces without an ambient. It is probably true by a standard argument, so it is a modest unpublished detail rather than a major discovery.

Line 1: 'se [-...-] définit' — the struck word appears to be 'étend' or similar; the rest is fine.
In the bracketed consequence the space is the script 𝒳 throughout: H^*(𝒳_strat, O_{𝒳_strat}) = H^*(𝒳, C).
The heavily struck line after 'triviale)' is illegible. It is followed by 'Ceci semble plausible, en regardant les "fibres formelles" des faisceaux…', with 'faisceaux' inserted above.
